title: Real erasure of a deleted message
description: Ryan 11-02: deletion must be real, so there are no privacy or retention issues later. Deleting a message removes its text from every place it can live: the channel record, mailbox items, Pi entries (which are immutable), compaction summaries that absorbed it, sub-agent conversations, bot memory and cost or activity records, S3 object versions (control-plane-stack.ts sets versioned: true on a bucket; confirm which), and DynamoDB backups. Design first: state what is erased at once, what expires and when, and what cannot be reached, such as a model provider's own retention. Spike with the channel record, because this is the riskiest unproven part of the plan and may change how bodies are stored in Pi logs. Done: design in docs, then Gherkin scenarios proving the text is gone from each store and that the bot no longer sees it.
